record.title: Set-Theoretic Cohen–Macaulay Ideals in Characteristic Zero
record.statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $R=K[w,x,y,z]$, and let $$\varphi:R\longrightarrow K[s^4,s^3t,st^3,t^4]$$ send $w,x,y,z$ to $s^4,s^3t,st^3,t^4$, respectively. Writing $\mathfrak{a}=\ker\varphi$, does there exist an ideal $\mathfrak{b}\subset R$ such that $\sqrt{\mathfrak{b}}=\mathfrak{a}$ and $R/\mathfrak{b}$ is Cohen–Macaulay?
record.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The characteristic-zero set-theoretic Cohen--Macaulay question is explicitly posed in the primary paper. Positive characteristic and several characteristic-zero classes are known, but no general ideal b with the required radical was found.

**Sources checked.**

- [original Oberwolfach Report 19/2005](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2005/19)
- [Singh--Walther, local cohomology and pure morphisms](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701524)
- [local cohomology of Du Bois singularities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02755)

This is a dated literature triage derived from the supplied OWR curation; verify time-sensitive status and cited claims independently.
